## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the timestamp’s meaning before merge. A process that has only started gets a completion timestamp, and the catalog also gives consumers an incorrect interpretation of NULL.

## Changes

The pull request adds `finished_at` to the current-state model and documents it in the schema catalog, while preserving one row per process based on the latest event. It also adds `review.txt`.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Align `finished_at` with the event it represents — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, `finished_at` reports `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z` as a completion time. The CASE selects the start timestamp, and the source defines only `created`, `started`, and `cleared` events. — Consumers using `finished_at` to count completed processes will include processes that have only started. — Fix: Use the event that represents completion, or rename the column and update the catalog if it is meant to expose a start time.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Document when the timestamp is NULL — For process 30, a `cleared` event after `started` makes `finished_at` NULL despite the earlier start. “NULL means the process has never been started” conflicts with `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` applied to the latest event. — Consumers following the catalog will misclassify previously started processes whose latest event is `cleared`.

## Suggestions

- models/schema.yml:12 — comments — Document the timestamp’s source offset — For a `started` event with `occurred_at` set to `2026-01-01T01:00:30+01:00`, the output retains `+01:00`. “Stored in UTC using the source event timestamp” conflicts with `then occurred_at`, which copies the value unchanged. — Consumers sorting the documented UTC strings can misorder timestamps with mixed offsets.
- models/processes.sql:10 — tests — Cover processes with only a `created` event — For process 10, the CASE should return NULL because its only event is `created`. The source fixture contains this input, but no test checks the resulting timestamp. — A regression that assigns the creation time to the new column would go undetected.
